bull.b: Acrivon’s AP3 platform provides a differentiated approach to precision oncology by linking drug response signatures with patient selection. If validated clinically, this model could improve development efficiency, support more targeted treatment decisions, and strengthen the strategic value of its investigational pipeline over multiple quarters.

Very low leverage and positive equity provide a financial buffer relative to a highly indebted development-stage company. This structure limits interest-related pressure and preserves flexibility to direct available capital toward clinical development, although it does not eliminate the need for future financing.

The continued support for the board and independent auditor indicates governance continuity during an important clinical-development period. Stable oversight can help maintain strategic focus, support execution of the pipeline, and provide organizational consistency while the company advances its platform and candidates.

bear.b: Acrivon remains dependent on investigational candidates because it has no reported product revenue or approved commercial medicines. This leaves operating performance tied to clinical and regulatory progress rather than recurring sales, increasing dependence on external capital until a program can generate durable commercial income.

Sustained operating and free-cash-flow deficits consume financial resources while the pipeline remains in development. Continued burn can reduce the company’s funding runway and force additional capital raises, potentially limiting development pace or requiring capital allocation decisions before clinical value is fully realized.

The enlarged equity incentive pool creates a multi-year source of potential dilution for existing shareholders, especially while the company has no recurring product revenue. Although equity awards may support hiring and retention, future share issuance can reduce each investor’s proportional ownership and increase financing sensitivity.
